predecessors.name: Regency of Algiers
predecessors.text: Algiers and nearby coastal points, entered by French troops on 5 July 1830

successors.name: French Africa
successors.text: Algeria as Cliopatria's French Africa row draws it from 1848, the year the Second Republic's constitution declared Algeria an integral part of France with three departments

ledger.x: 5 July 1830: French troops enter Algiers and the dey capitulates.
1832: the French occupy Bône.
1833: Bougie falls.
1833: Oran and the coast to Arzew and Mostaganem pass under French control.
1834: the annexed 'area of limited occupation near the coast' is wider than the Algiers radius.

22 July 1834: a royal ordinance organises the occupied territories and is generally treated as the formal annexation of Algeria: the occupied coast becomes a colony under a governor-general answerable to the war minister.
January 1836: the French take Tlemcen.
30 May 1837: the Treaty of Tafna.
13 October 1837: Valée storms Constantine.
Late 1839: the war resumes.
1839: Blida is captured.
1840: Miliana is occupied.
1840: the Sétif country of the Algiers-Constantine belt is held.
1840: the coast and country around Constantine are held.
1841: Mascara comes under full French control.
1842: Tlemcen and the Oran interior pass to France.
March 1844: the Saharan expedition starts from Biskra under the Duke of Aumale, a 22-year-old general.
19 June 1844: Bugeaud occupies Oujda.

18 March 1845: the Treaty of Lalla Maghnia fixes the frontier from the Mediterranean to Teniet el-Sassi, some seventy miles inland (after the Treaty of Tangier of 10 September 1844, in which Morocco recognised Algeria as part of the French Empire and outlawed Abd al-Qadir): Yich and Figuig to Morocco; Aïn Séfra…
1846: the French row jumps from 48,573 to 211,876 km2.
23 December 1847: Abd al-Qadir surrenders.
End of 1847: the conquest is complete and the colony passes into France.

wars.name: Invasion of Algiers in 1830
wars.outcome: About 34,000 French troops land at Sidi Ferruch on 14 June 1830, win at Staouéli on 19 June and enter Algiers on 5 July; the dey capitulates and leaves for Italy.

wars.name: French conquest of Algeria
wars.outcome: France annexes the occupied coast in 1834, signs the Treaty of Tafna in 1837, storms Constantine in 1837, resumes the war in late 1839, takes the emir's smala in 1843, defeats Morocco in 1844 and forces Abd al-Qadir's surrender on 23 December 1847.

wars.name: Siege of Constantine (1837)
wars.outcome: Clauzel's column is repulsed in November 1836; Damrémont is killed in the 1837 siege and Valée storms the city on 13 October 1837.

wars.name: First Franco-Moroccan War
wars.outcome: French victory: Oujda occupied 19 June 1844, Tangier bombarded 6 August, Isly won 14 August, Mogador taken 16 August; the Treaty of Tangier (10 September 1844) ends the war and the Treaty of Lalla Maghnia (18 March 1845) sets the frontier from the sea to…

certainty.note: French control is coast, towns and columns' reach: the 1830-1836 "limited occupation" is a string of garrisoned places and the interior was the emir's or Constantine's.

The frontier with Morocco is sharp from 18 March 1845 (the Treaty of Lalla Maghnia, from the Mediterranean to Teniet el-Sassi); south of Figuig it was left undelimited, the Saharan edge and the frontier with Tunis were undefined, and…
